themes_detail.label: Dead Trees Crisis in Parks
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints spiked to 4 THIS WEEK—a 1500% increase versus the 8-week baseline of 0.2 complaints per week (z-score: 8.66)—suggesting either a sudden die-off event or increased resident awareness of an existing problem that demands immediate Parks Department investigation.
evidence: 4 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 8.66 indicates statistically extreme deviation (severity: high)
Aligns with community board's standing request for park upgrades and maintenance
reporting_angles: Are disease, pests, or weather events killing trees faster than Parks can respond?
How many trees are at risk across Washington Heights / Inwood parks, and what is the replacement timeline?

themes_detail.label: Encampment Surge in Public Spaces
themes_detail.summary: Homeless encampment complaints jumped to 12 LAST WEEK—an 1100% spike from the 8-week baseline of 1.0 complaint per week (z-score: 6.63)—indicating either a rapid influx of unhoused people or a tipping point in visible street homelessness that residents can no longer ignore.
evidence: 12 encampment complaints LAST WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.63 marks this as a severe statistical outlier
Community board has repeatedly requested enhanced park safety and security staff—suggests long-standing capacity gap
reporting_angles: Where are encampments concentrated, and what triggered the sudden increase?
Are city outreach and shelter services equipped to respond, or are residents left managing the fallout?

themes_detail.label: Lot Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Vacant lot complaints exploded to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO—a 2300% spike from the 8-week baseline of 0.1 complaints per week (z-score: 8.69)—signaling rapid blight accumulation or negligent property maintenance that may correlate with the encampment surge.
evidence: 3 lot condition complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 8.69 indicates extreme statistical deviation (severity: high)
May overlap with encampment complaints if vacant lots are becoming de facto shelter sites
reporting_angles: Which specific lots are deteriorating, and who owns them?
Are city agencies (DSNY, HPD, Parks) enforcing maintenance or are private owners sidestepping responsibility?

themes_detail.label: Park Rule Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Violations of park rules jumped to 4 LAST WEEK—a 540% increase from the 8-week baseline of 0.6 complaints per week (z-score: 4.85)—suggesting either breakdown in park enforcement, increased illicit activity, or resident frustration with conditions that correlates with the encampment and dead-tree crises.
evidence: 4 park rule violation complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 4.85 marks this as a severe outlier
Community board's standing request for enhanced park safety and security staff indicates prior awareness of enforcement gaps
reporting_angles: What specific park rules are being violated (after-hours use, littering, substance use)?
Is Parks Enforcement Patrol staffing adequate to respond to encampments and rule violations simultaneously?

themes_detail.label: Smoking/Vaping in Parks Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Smoking or vaping complaints rose to 11 LAST WEEK—a 151% increase from the 8-week baseline of 4.4 complaints per week (z-score: 5.03)—indicating either increased indoor/park smoking enforcement awareness or degradation of park air quality and user experience.
evidence: 11 smoking/vaping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 4.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 5.03 indicates statistically significant spike (severity: high)
May reflect increased park usage or resident sensitivity given encampment-related park degradation
reporting_angles: Are park users smoking in violation of city rules, or is this a specific park location problem?
Is this a byproduct of encampment activity or a separate enforcement issue?
